facts.text: Stonington was named after North Stonington, Connecticut, by settlers who laid out a 160‑acre town site in the early 1830s.
The original settlers traveled south from Connecticut, choosing land near present‑day Stonington after finding no single tract large enough in the surrounding counties.

In 1833 Thomas P. Chapman visited Illinois to visit relatives in Fulton, Warren, and Knox Counties, marking the first recorded arrival of a Connecticut settler in the area that would become Stonington.
Stonington sits in Christian County, Illinois, a detail that ties the village to the county’s broader historical narrative.
On December 1, 2018, an EF2 tornado struck the western part of Stonington, but fortunately no injuries or deaths were reported.
The village’s founding colony was part of a larger migration that included travel by railroad, riverboat, and wagon across the prairie.
